transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-07
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Dylan Wu (Redwood CSM), Jordan Lee (Mira Head of ML), Samir Patel (Infra), Lee Harrold (Product), Taylor Kim (Data Scientist)

Summary: quick walkthrough of Redwood Console's canary + rollback playbook, demo of A/B traffic split and prompt-set regression alerts. Customer focused on safe rollouts, false-positive tuning for regression alerts, and how to run synthetic canaries with private deployments.

Topics covered: Redwood Console canary flows, Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching/quant, A/B comparison UI, how regression alerts tie to prompt sets, synthetic traffic generation tips, RBAC for canary traffic, audit logs and SSO notes.

--- Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcribed by Fireflies.ai — may include errors) ---
[00:00] Alex: Cool good afternoon everyone, I'm Alex from Redwood, thanks for carving out time. We brought Priya from the SE team to run through our canary and rollback playbook and show the A/B benchmarking flow.
[00:12] Jordan: Hey Alex thanks. We're mid-peak for a rollout so trying to get the safety checks nailed down. Especially: we need deterministic criteria to abort a rollout if prompt quality degrades.
[00:20] Priya: Totally, that's exactly what we'll show — the prompt-sets + regression alerting, and then the canary gating logic. By the end we want you to have a concrete checklist you can automate.
[00:29] Samir: Quick infra context — Mira has a mix of Dedicated GPUs for steady inference and hosted for burst, and most of our sensitive traffic goes over the VPC. We also have an on-prem test cluster.
[00:38] Alex: Great, that gives us an idea. We'll cover both Hosted and Private flows — note the RBAC differences and how audit logs are surfaced in the Console.
[00:46] Lee: One constraint — we need the canary to run against synthetic traffic and also a small percentage of live traffic, like 1%. We want to catch regressions in composition and hallucinations.
[00:56] Priya: Good — our A/B split supports hybrid routing. We can route 1% live, 99% synthetic. You can use the traffic replay utility in the Console or bring your own script.
[01:07] Taylor: Fwiw we have pre-built intents; we can share a sample prompt set — about 120 prompts across core intents.
[01:13] Priya: Perfect, that's the right size. We'll show how to attach that prompt set to a regression alert and tune thresholds.

[01:30] Priya: Ok jumping into the Console — first the canary workflow. Step one: create a canary policy — choose the model variant (we show a quantized variant for cost), split percentages, success criteria. The UI will show projected token cost based on sample traffic.
[01:46] [screen share noise]
[01:50] Priya: Here I'm creating a canary called "mira-canary-1". Notice the automatic guardrail suggestions from Redwood Optimize — it recommends a batch size of 8 and short KV cache TTL for these short prompts to save latency.
[02:04] Jordan: Wait, batch size 8 — do we control that per route or per model?
[02:08] Priya: Per route — so you can have different batching for conversational vs. single-turn widgets. Also the Optimize tab will surface quantization options if your workload is latency tolerant.
[02:16] Samir: Does the canary run inside our VPC when we choose Private? We need to ensure KMS access is local.
[02:21] Alex: Yes — for Private deployments the canary traffic stays in your VPC; the control plane still shows the results but no payload is retained by Redwood. KMS integrations are supported for key wrapping.

[02:35] Priya: Next step, defining success criteria — you can set a combination of metrics: mean token latency, top-k accuracy (if you have labeled data), hallucination rate (we call out heuristics), and custom scoring functions uploaded as a lambda.
[02:50] Taylor: Custom scoring function — that's our main ask. We compute a domain-specific relevance score and want that to be part of the canary gate.
[02:56] Priya: You can upload a scoring container or use the serverless scorer. We run that scorer against both baseline and candidate and Redwood computes uplift and shows a statistical test.
[03:08] [muttered]
[03:12] Priya: Important: the Console uses bootstrapped confidence intervals — so small sample sizes will be labeled as low confidence and you'll see a warning.

[03:25] Alex: Let's demo an A/B run quickly — we'll compare your current production model (mdl-prod-v3) vs candidate (mdl-llm-quant-v4). We'll do a 50/50 split for the synthetic run and then show the A/B compare report.
[03:39] [screen share: launching an A/B job]
[03:44] Priya: Feeding the Mira prompt set — note the transcripts show exact prompts and masked PII automatically. There's also a replay ID so you can correlate to logs.
[03:55] Alex: We're going to flag two alert types: quality regression (prompt-level score delta) and severity-level hallucinations (open-ended generation that fails the pattern tests).

[04:10] Taylor: Real quick — earlier you said the KV... KV cash?
[04:13] Priya: (laughs) KV cache, yes. The caching behavior affects latency a lot; in canaries we often disable long-lived KV caching so we get fresh evaluation for generation variance.

[04:25] [00:04:25 - short pause while redwood console updates]
[04:42] Priya: The A/B summary is ready — showing per-prompt difference heatmap. You can filter by tag, intent, or failure reason. Here you can see two clusters where the candidate has higher hallucination heuristics.
[04:59] Jordan: Can we set the threshold so that any intent with >5% increase in hallucination auto-fails the canary?
[05:05] Priya: Absolutely — you can set fail conditions at the intent-level. Also you can add a manual gate that sends to a Slack channel or PagerDuty before aborting.

[05:20] Samir: How about false positives on alerts — we don't want noisy aborts. What's the tuning surface?
[05:26] Alex: There's a couple: you can tune the sensitivity in the heuristic, require sustained degradation over N minutes, or require multiple metric hits (latency + quality). We also support a cooldown window and a minimum sample size.

[05:42] Priya: Let me show the regression alert config. Under Alerts -> Regression you can pick metrics, rollup window, and an isolation mode. Isolation will try to find which prompt clusters trigger the alert to reduce noise.
[05:55] Taylor: Nice. Does the isolation use embeddings or lexical matching?
[05:58] Priya: Both — it uses an ensemble: semantic embeddings to cluster and lexical diffs to highlight template mismatches. Sometimes the transcriber mixes up model names though in the logs, you'll see "mdl-quick" instead of the actual model.

[06:12] [background cross-talk]
[06:18] Priya: For A/B comparisons we also compute an uplift p-value. If your team requires stricter stats, you can plug in your own evaluation harness outputs via the API.

[06:30] Alex: I want to cover the rollback playbook because that's critical. By default Redwood supports automated rollback once a canary fails the gating criteria. You can choose an automatic rollback or a manual review. The playbook includes an automated mitigation path: reduce traffic to candidate to 0, spin up fallback model, and open a ticket in your ticketing system.
[06:49] Jordan: For compliance we need an audit trail for every rollback event — who triggered it and why.
[06:54] Priya: The Console logs every rollout and rollback as immutable events with the diff of config, who initiated it (SSO identity), and the exact metric state at time of rollback. Those logs are exportable to S3 or your SIEM.

[07:08] Samir: How about canary cost — if we run 1% of live at peak that could be pricey.
[07:14] Alex: We surface a projected token cost before starting. Redwood Optimize can also suggest a cheaper quantized variant for the candidate, or recommend switching to batch mode during off-peak. There's also a burst policy so you can cap spend.

[07:28] [screen noise: switching page]
[07:33] Priya: Now I'll show the playbook export — this is the human step checklist. It includes pre-checks (alerts configured, sample size verified), synthetic generation run, threshold pass/fail, and rollback steps. You can convert it to a runbook that integrates with your CI (we have a GitHub Actions template).
[07:51] Lee: Do you have examples of playbooks used by other customers? We might need a template for legal to review.
[07:57] Dylan (CSM): Yep — I'll share anonymized playbooks, and also a sample of audit logs for SOC2 review.

[08:08] Taylor: We use an internal metric called "user-visible error" — essentially a binary label we have on historical responses. Can Redwood ingest that and surface it as a KPI?
[08:16] Priya: Yes, you can upload historical labels and map them to prompts. We then show precision/recall and compute lift in those terms. That mapping can be part of the canary gate.

[08:28] Jordan: Security: SSO—we need SAML and role-based restrictions so only two of us can abort a canary. Also need to see how long logs are retained.
[08:37] Alex: We support SAML SSO, fine-grained RBAC, and exportable audit logs. Retention is configurable per contract. For Private deployments you can keep logs on-prem.

[08:50] [short pause]
[09:02] Priya: I'm going to trigger a simulated live hybrid canary now — 1% live + synthetic. Notice the live requests are tagged and the console obscures PII.
[09:12] [console updates, stuttering due to screen share]
[09:25] Priya: Alright, the canary is running. On the right you can see the live traffic stream and synthetic stream separate. We also surface rolling dq metrics.
[09:36] Alex: While that's running, a quick note on API-driven automation — everything we just clicked in the Console has an equivalent API call so you can put it into your CI. The SDK snippet is in the docs.
[09:46] Samir: That will help. We want to trigger canaries as part of the weekday deploy pipeline.

[10:00] [10:00 - 18:00] (system: longer period of A/B run and results generation; transcript samples every ~30s)
[10:00] Priya: The A/B job completed. Here's the A/B report. Candidate shows a 3.8% increase in hallucination heuristic across the full set, but some intents show no change.
[10:14] Taylor: Can you slice by device type? Some dialogs are mobile-only.
[10:18] Priya: Yes, you can add dimensions — we also show latency percentiles per device, region, and tenant id.
[10:28] Jordan: In the heatmap I'm seeing a cluster of prompts with the biggest delta; can we open a deep view on those?
[10:33] Priya: Opening it now — you can see prompt text, candidate response, baseline response, scoring detail and the scorer's rationale. For the biggest failure the candidate hallucinated a nonexistent entity. We flag source-of-truth checks if you have grounding data.
[10:53] Samir: Is grounding implemented server-side or do we have to call an external fetch?
[10:58] Priya: Both patterns supported. You can call your external knowledge service in the scoring step or enable Redwood's grounding prefetch if you're on Dedicated. It's configurable.

[11:12] Jordan: So based on this report, if we set the canary to auto-abort on >2% absolute uplift in hallucination, it'll flip to rollback?
[11:20] Alex: Correct — assuming your sample size meets the minimum confidence. You can also add a manual review step that pages the on-call and waits for approval before rollback.

[11:32] Lee: Two policy questions: 1) we want an exception policy so certain high-value intents are allowed a bit more drift, 2) we need a way to tag a run as "experimental" so it doesn't trigger customer-facing alerts.
[11:45] Priya: Both supported. You can tag intents and set per-intent thresholds, and experimental runs are labelled and excluded from SLA-level alerts by default.

[11:55] Taylor: One more: can we do post-rollout monitoring with longer windows? We want to catch slow drift that occurs over weeks.
[11:62] Priya: (laughs) small timestamp hiccup — sure. We have drift monitors that run daily and use rolling windows; they can auto-create regression alerts if gradual degradation is detected.

[12:12] Alex: Ok we'll wrap with a short recap and next steps.
[12:16] Alex: Recap: 1) Priya demoed canary creation, metric gating, and A/B reports. 2) Automatic rollback and manual gates explained. 3) Tuning surfaces for false positive reduction (sample size, composite metrics, cooldown). 4) Audit/tracing and SAML/RBAC options available.
[12:33] Jordan: This is useful — next for us is to run a 2-week pilot: synthetic + 1% live traffic, with the scoring function we use. We'll also want a cost estimate.
[12:44] Alex: Great — action items and Dylan will follow up with artifacts. Priya will share the replay script and a GitHub Action template for running canaries.
[12:55] Samir: Quick logistics — we need a Private demo instance to test KMS and VPC behavior.
[13:01] Dylan: We'll provision a Private trial and loop in infra.
[13:06] Jordan: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[13:09] Alex: Thanks, we'll send the playbook and recording.

[13:20] [call ends]

Notes: occasional transcription errors present (timestamps, small word swaps). Links & artifacts to be shared: playbook PDF, demo recording, synthetic traffic sample script (Python), SOC2 audit snippet, pricing estimate.
